Subject: Re: Order form pricing exhibit — initial ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending over the Exhibit C draft. We reviewed it with procurement and legal — overall promising, but we have three areas we need clarified before we can move to our finance review:

1) Cap smoothing: the top-line cap moves quickly relative to expected monthly run-rate growth. Can you propose an intermediate stabilizer (6–12 month smoothing) instead of a hard jump at month 13?

2) Floor protection: we need a hard floor for the first 12 months tied to a minimum committed spend rather than a percentage of forecast.

3) True-up mechanics: if our usage exceeds the cap band, the true-up timing needs to align with our quarterly billing cycle (45 days after quarter close) rather than 30 days.

Attached is a marked PDF (Novus-exhibitC-redline.pdf) with inline notes from legal. Gwen flagged the standard indemnity cross-ref in section 4 as well — she'll follow up if that needs legal-to-legal discussion.

Appreciate a chewable proposal with specific language we can share internally by next Thursday (7/18).

Best,
Samantha
Head of Procurement
Novus Health

Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and the PDF. We can do all three items but want to align on tradeoffs so the proposal is operationally realistic. Quick clarifying points: 

• For the cap stabilizer: are you thinking a linear smoothing (equal step-ups each month) or a two-phase cap (flat then step)? Either is possible but has different billing/forecasting implications.

• For the floor: specifying a dollar minimum for the first 12 months is fine. Can you confirm whether Novus will consider a minimum committed token bucket or prefer a spend-based minimum?

• True-up timing: 45 days after quarter close is acceptable; we'll update the terms and show the impact in the attached spreadsheet.

We're pulling together a proposed Exhibit C with both language and an illustrative amortization table. I’ll send a draft to you and Gwen by 7/17 EOD.

Marissa / team — reviewed Novus’ edits and drafted language options. High-level guidance below; I attached a Word snippet (MA-Orderform-v3.docx) with inline redlines for Exhibit C.

1) Cap smoothing: Recommend the two-phase approach — Month 1–12: fixed monthly cap equal to 60% of year-1 forecast; Months 13–24: stepped increase to full committed cap with quarterly review. Why: it limits immediate exposure while giving Novus predictability. We can offer the linear alternative at a modest operational premium (one-time implementation credit).

2) Floor protection: Propose a dollar-denominated minimum for months 1–12 ("Minimum Annual Commit" equal to 30% of year-1 committed spend), with a credit mechanism if Novus underutilizes. Language included clarifies that credits are applied on the first post-quarter invoice.

3) True-up timing: Agree to Q+45 days. Update terms to specify invoice adjustments and a single reconciliation run per quarter to avoid multiple micro-adjustments.

Operational note: billing needs a flag on the order that toggles smoothing vs standard cap to prevent double-charges. Ops must confirm availability; asking billing to confirm by Monday.

If legal is comfortable with the proposed indemnity cross-ref limits, we can finalize language and send it to Novus with the pricing delta.

— Karthik
Head of Legal (Contracts) | Redwood Inference

Subject: Order Form update: cap/floor harmonization proposal and program impact

Samantha / Gwen — thank you for the quick turnaround and the redline. Per our internal review we’ve proposed a harmonized Exhibit C that aims to balance Novus’ predictability needs with Redwood’s operational and revenue protections. Summary below and attached: MA-Orderform-v3.docx (redline) + pricing delta workbook.

Summary of what we propose:
• Cap: two-phase approach — Months 1–12 a fixed monthly cap at 60% of year-1 forecast; Months 13–24 step to full committed cap with quarterly ramps. This provides smoothing while preserving runway for Redwood.
• Floor: a dollar-denominated Minimum Annual Commit for year 1 equal to 30% of committed spend, with an underutilization credit applied on the first post-quarter invoice.
• True-up: alignment to Q+45 days with a single reconciliation run per quarter.

Pricing impact: Ben’s workbook shows the two-phase smoothing reduces immediate exposure vs a linear smoothing. We included an optional one-time implementation credit to cover the operational cost of a bespoke billing flag if Novus prefers linear smoothing.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Gwen/legal: confirm the indemnity cross-ref language in section 4 of the MA-Orderform-v3.docx. If acceptable, sign-off for redline circulation.
2) Novus: confirm whether you prefer the two-phase smoothing or the linear alternative (we’ve priced both). If two-phase, we’ll prepare a final Exhibit C and updated order form for signatures by 7/28.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the workbook.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
